```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE,
  warning = FALSE,
  message = FALSE,
  fig.align = "center")

# Load required libraries
library(sf)
library(spdep)
library(gstat)
library(ggplot2)
library(viridis)
library(dplyr)

set.seed(7002)

```

1. Environment Initialization and Spatial Data Import

This section constructs a simulated spatial dataset representing 35 districts in Uganda. Each district is assigned mock attributes for Banana Xanthomonas Wilt (BXW) incidence and phenotypic performance (bunch weight).

```{r }
n_districts <- 35

# Construct mock polygon geometries
polys <- lapply(1:n_districts, function(i) {
  center <- c(32.5 + runif(1, -0.6, 0.6), 1.4 + runif(1, -0.5, 0.5))
  r <- runif(1, 0.2, 0.5)
  pts <- cbind(
    center[1] + r * cos(seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = 6)),
    center[2] + r * sin(seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = 6))
  )
  st_polygon(list(rbind(pts, pts[1, ])))
})

uganda_districts <- st_sf(
  District_ID          = 1:n_districts,
  District_Name        = paste("District", 1:n_districts),
  BXW_Incidence_Index  = runif(n_districts, min = 5.0, max = 85.0),
  Bunch_Weight_KG      = runif(n_districts, min = 12.0, max = 45.0),
  Stunting_Rate_Pct    = runif(n_districts, min = 12.5, max = 48.0),
  geometry             = st_sfc(polys, crs = 4326)
)

# Disable S2 for planar contiguity calculations
sf_use_s2(FALSE)

# Construct spatial neighbours (Queen contiguity with snapping)
district_neighbors <- poly2nb(uganda_districts, queen = TRUE, snap = 0.1)

# Row-standardised spatial weights matrix
spatial_weights_w <- nb2listw(district_neighbors, style = "W", zero.policy = TRUE)

# Re-enable S2
sf_use_s2(TRUE)

# Preview the spatial object
print(uganda_districts)

```

2. Global Spatial Autocorrelation Diagnostic (Moran's I)

We test the null hypothesis of Complete Spatial Randomness (CSR) for the BXW Incidence Index using Global Moran's I.

```{r }

moran_diagnostic <- moran.test(
  uganda_districts$BXW_Incidence_Index,
  listw = spatial_weights_w,
  zero.policy = TRUE
)

cat("Global Moran's I Statistic :", round(moran_diagnostic$estimate[1], 4), "\n")
cat("Expectation under CSR      :", round(moran_diagnostic$estimate[2], 4), "\n")
cat("P-value                    :", round(moran_diagnostic$p.value, 5), "\n")

moran_diagnostic

```
Interpretation

A statistically significant positive Moran's I indicates spatial clustering of BXW incidence (high-incidence districts tend to be neighbours of other high-incidence districts).

3. Spatial Interpolation of Phenotypic Performance (IDW)

Inverse Distance Weighting (IDW) is used to predict bunch weight at unmonitored locations across the study area.

```{r }

sf_use_s2(FALSE)

# Extract district centroids as trial stations
suppressWarnings({
  trial_stations <- st_centroid(uganda_districts)
})

# Create a regular grid over the study area
raw_grid <- st_make_grid(uganda_districts, n = c(50, 50))
spatial_grid_sf <- st_sf(geometry = raw_grid)

# Retain only grid cells that intersect the districts
spatial_grid <- st_filter(spatial_grid_sf, uganda_districts)

# Perform IDW interpolation (power = 2)
idw_model <- idw(
  formula   = Bunch_Weight_KG ~ 1,
  locations = trial_stations,
  newdata   = spatial_grid,
  idp       = 2.0
)

# Attach predicted values
spatial_grid$Estimated_Yield_KG <- idw_model$var1.pred

cat("\n--- IDW Predicted Yield Summary (KG) ---\n")
print(summary(spatial_grid$Estimated_Yield_KG))

sf_use_s2(TRUE)

```

4. IDW Prediction Surface Map

This map shows the continuous spatial prediction of bunch weight (kg) generated by Inverse Distance Weighting.
```{r }

sf_use_s2(FALSE)

idw_map <- ggplot() +
  # Predicted continuous surface
  geom_sf(data = spatial_grid, aes(fill = Estimated_Yield_KG), color = NA) +
  
  # District boundaries for reference
  geom_sf(data = uganda_districts, fill = NA, color = "white", linewidth = 0.4) +
  
  # Trial station locations
  geom_sf(data = trial_stations, color = "black", size = 2, shape = 18) +
  
  # Continuous colour scale
  scale_fill_viridis_c(
    option    = "viridis",
    name      = "Predicted\nBunch Weight (kg)",
    direction = 1
  ) +
  
  labs(
    title    = "IDW Spatial Interpolation of Phenotypic Performance",
    subtitle = "Predicted Banana Bunch Weight (kg) Across Target Districts",
    caption  = "Method: Inverse Distance Weighting (power = 2) | CRS: WGS 84"
  ) +
  
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    plot.title       = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13),
    plot.subtitle    = element_text(size = 9, colour = "#4a4a4a", margin = margin(b = 8)),
    legend.position  = "right",
    legend.title     = element_text(face = "bold", size = 9),
    axis.title       = element_blank(),
    axis.text        = element_text(size = 7, colour = "#666666"),
    panel.grid.major = element_line(colour = "#e0e0e0", linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.2)
  )

print(idw_map)

sf_use_s2(TRUE)
```

5. Local Moran’s I (LISA) Cluster Map

Local Indicators of Spatial Association (LISA) identify statistically significant spatial clusters and spatial outliers of BXW incidence.

```{r }

sf_use_s2(FALSE)

# Compute Local Moran’s I
local_moran <- localmoran(
  uganda_districts$BXW_Incidence_Index,
  listw = spatial_weights_w,
  zero.policy = TRUE
)

# Extract local statistics and p-values
uganda_districts$Ii    <- local_moran[, "Ii"]
uganda_districts$Pr_Ii <- local_moran[, "Pr(z != E(Ii))"]

# Create LISA cluster categories
mean_bxw <- mean(uganda_districts$BXW_Incidence_Index, na.rm = TRUE)
uganda_districts$centred_bxw <- uganda_districts$BXW_Incidence_Index - mean_bxw

# Spatial lag of the centred variable
uganda_districts$lag_bxw <- lag.listw(
  spatial_weights_w,
  uganda_districts$centred_bxw,
  zero.policy = TRUE
)

# Assign LISA cluster types
uganda_districts$LISA_cluster <- "Not Significant"
sig <- which(uganda_districts$Pr_Ii < 0.05)

uganda_districts$LISA_cluster[sig] <- dplyr::case_when(
  uganda_districts$centred_bxw[sig] > 0 & uganda_districts$lag_bxw[sig] > 0 ~ "High-High",
  uganda_districts$centred_bxw[sig] < 0 & uganda_districts$lag_bxw[sig] < 0 ~ "Low-Low",
  uganda_districts$centred_bxw[sig] > 0 & uganda_districts$lag_bxw[sig] < 0 ~ "High-Low",
  uganda_districts$centred_bxw[sig] < 0 & uganda_districts$lag_bxw[sig] > 0 ~ "Low-High",
  TRUE ~ "Not Significant"
)

# Order the factor levels for consistent colours
uganda_districts$LISA_cluster <- factor(
  uganda_districts$LISA_cluster,
  levels = c("High-High", "Low-Low", "High-Low", "Low-High", "Not Significant")
)

# Summary of cluster counts
cat("\nLISA Cluster Summary:\n")
print(table(uganda_districts$LISA_cluster))

```
```{r }

# Colour palette for LISA clusters (classic red-blue scheme)
lisa_colours <- c(
  "High-High"       = "#d7191c",
  "Low-Low"         = "#2c7bb6",
  "High-Low"        = "#fdae61",
  "Low-High"        = "#abd9e9",
  "Not Significant" = "#f0f0f0"
)

lisa_map <- ggplot(data = uganda_districts) +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = LISA_cluster), color = "white", linewidth = 0.35) +
  
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = lisa_colours,
    name   = "LISA Cluster",
    drop   = FALSE
  ) +
  
  labs(
    title    = "Local Moran’s I Cluster Map – BXW Incidence",
    subtitle = "Spatial Clusters and Outliers of Banana Xanthomonas Wilt Incidence",
    caption  = "Significance level: p < 0.05 | Queen contiguity spatial weights"
  ) +
  
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    plot.title       = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13),
    plot.subtitle    = element_text(size = 9, colour = "#4a4a4a", margin = margin(b = 8)),
    legend.position  = "right",
    legend.title     = element_text(face = "bold", size = 9),
    axis.title       = element_blank(),
    axis.text        = element_text(size = 7, colour = "#666666"),
    panel.grid.major = element_line(colour = "#e0e0e0", linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.2)
  )

print(lisa_map)
#ggsave("output/lisa_map.png", plot = lisa_map_plot, dpi = 300)

sf_use_s2(TRUE)
```
